svg.title: Propagating a deadline budget through a call chain
svg.desc: A timeline from 0 to 2,000 milliseconds. The client gives the TaskFlow API a 2,000 millisecond budget. The API spends 200 milliseconds on its own work, then calls the tasks service and passes the remaining budget minus a 50 millisecond margin, 1,750 milliseconds, in a request header. The tasks service spends 250 milliseconds, then queries the database with the remaining 1,450 milliseconds after its own margin. The query takes 300 milliseconds, so everything finishes well inside the deadline. If the work cannot finish, every hop stops at or before the 2,000 millisecond deadline, when the caller gives up anyway. Without propagation, each hop uses its own fixed timeout, such as 5 seconds, so the tasks service and the database keep working long after the API has already answered with an error at 2 seconds.

g.text: One request, one budget: each hop gets what is left, minus a margin
2,000 ms: the caller gives up anyway
Without propagation: every hop has its own fixed 5 s timeout
The API answers 504 at 2 s, but tasks and the database keep working for up to 5 s more on a
request nobody is waiting for. Under overload that wasted work is what keeps the system down.
Inner timeouts must fit inside outer ones; pass the remaining budget, not a fixed number.
